position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that fails to support, or betrays, a friend, employer or country.
examples: He was fired for acting *disloyally* toward the company.
She felt her brother had behaved *disloyally* by taking their father's side.
Nobody on the team wanted to be caught speaking *disloyally* about the coach.

position: end — after the verb, most often *fail*; before its word with adjectives (*dismally low*)

senses.gloss: Very badly; in a way that is a complete failure.
examples: The plan failed *dismally*.
Turnout was *dismally* low this year.
Our team played *dismally* in the second half.

senses.gloss: In a gloomy, unhappy way.
examples: "It's raining again," he said *dismally*.
She stared *dismally* at the pile of bills.

position: end — usually after *speak*, *talk* or *write*, before *of* or *about*

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you think someone or something has little value or importance.
examples: He spoke *disparagingly* of his former boss.
Critics wrote *disparagingly* about the remake.
She referred *disparagingly* to the plan as a "wish list."

position: end — after the verb or its object

senses.gloss: Calmly and fairly, without letting personal feelings take over.
examples: A judge has to weigh the evidence *dispassionately*.
She described the accident *dispassionately*, as if it had happened to someone else.
Try to look at the numbers *dispassionately*.

position: before its word — before a participle or adjective (*disproportionately affected*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: Much more or much less than is fair or expected compared with others.
examples: Low-income families are *disproportionately* affected by the tax.
Rents have risen *disproportionately* in the city center.
The company spends *disproportionately* on marketing.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: Rudely, without showing proper respect.
examples: He was suspended for speaking *disrespectfully* to a teacher.
Please don't talk about your grandmother so *disrespectfully*.
A few fans behaved *disrespectfully* during the national anthem.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that interrupts or disturbs what other people are doing.
examples: Students who behave *disruptively* will be asked to leave.
A phone rang *disruptively* in the middle of the ceremony.
The protesters acted *disruptively* but peacefully.

position: end — after verbs like *smile* and *answer*; before its word in *distantly related*

senses.gloss: Far away, or not closely connected.
examples: We're *distantly* related through my mother's side.
A dog barked *distantly* somewhere across the field.

senses.gloss: In a cool, unfriendly way that keeps people at a distance.
examples: She smiled *distantly* and kept walking.
He answered *distantly*, clearly thinking about something else.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (*distinctively American*); end after a verb
contrast: Do not confuse with *distinctly* 'clearly, noticeably': *a distinctly cold room* is noticeably cold, while *a distinctively designed room* has its own recognizable style.

senses.gloss: In a way that is typical of one person, place or thing and makes it easy to recognize.
examples: The song has a *distinctively* Southern sound.
Her handwriting is *distinctively* round and neat.
The coffee has a *distinctively* smoky flavor.

position: mid or end — with *remember*, *hear*, *say*; before its word with adjectives (*distinctly odd*)
modifies: verbs of perceiving, speaking and remembering; adjectives
contrast: Not the same as *distinctively* 'in a characteristic, recognizable way' — see that entry.

senses.gloss: Clearly, so that it is easy to hear, see or remember.
examples: I *distinctly* remember locking the door.
Speak slowly and *distinctly* into the microphone.
I *distinctly* heard her say no.

senses.gloss: Noticeably; definitely.
examples: The room felt *distinctly* colder after sunset.
His tone was *distinctly* unfriendly.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without paying full attention, because you are thinking about something else.
examples: He nodded *distractedly* while scrolling through his phone.
She *distractedly* stirred her coffee.
"Sure, sure," he said *distractedly*.

position: before its word — before an adjective; front as a comment on the whole sentence

senses.gloss: To a degree that is upsetting or worrying.
examples: The error rate remains *distressingly* high.
Cases like this are *distressingly* common.
*Distressingly*, nobody called the police.

position: before its word — before an adjective or adverb; front as a comment on the whole sentence
modifies: adjectives, adverbs, or a whole sentence

senses.gloss: In a way or to a degree that is worrying or upsetting.
examples: The movie is *disturbingly* realistic.
The number of overdoses has risen *disturbingly* fast.
*Disturbingly*, the files were left on an open server.

position: before its word — before a participle (*divinely inspired*)

senses.gloss: By God or a god; as an act of heaven.
examples: Many believers see the text as *divinely* inspired.
Kings once claimed they were *divinely* appointed to rule.
She felt her recovery had been *divinely* guided.

position: end — after the verb
contrast: *Dizzily* describes how someone who feels dizzy moves, or how things spin around them. For something that makes you dizzy, like a height or a pace, Americans say *dizzyingly*: *dizzyingly high*, not *dizzily high*.

senses.gloss: In an unsteady way, with a spinning feeling in your head.
examples: He stood up too fast and swayed *dizzily*.
The room spun *dizzily* around her.
The kids staggered *dizzily* off the merry-go-round.

position: mid or end
form: -ly from *dogged* 'stubbornly determined', said in two syllables

senses.gloss: With stubborn determination, refusing to give up.
examples: She *doggedly* pursued the story for two years.
The team fought *doggedly* until the final whistle.
He worked *doggedly* through the pile of paperwork.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs of saying, believing and applying rules

senses.gloss: In a way that insists your beliefs are right and refuses to consider other views.
examples: He *dogmatically* refused to consider any other diet.
Don't apply the rules too *dogmatically*.
She argued *dogmatically* that there was only one right answer.

position: end — after the verb or its object; before its word with participles (*domestically produced*)
contrast: Russian *домашний* 'home' can mislead: *domestically* almost always means 'inside the country' — *domestically produced* means made in this country, not made at home.

senses.gloss: Inside a country, as opposed to abroad.
examples: Most of the cars are sold *domestically*.
The airline flies *domestically* and to Canada.
We only buy *domestically* grown produce.

position: end — after the verb or its object
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *double*
contrast: After a verb the adverb stays flat: *pay double*, not *pay doubly*. *Doubly* goes before an adjective and means 'twice as': *doubly important*.

senses.gloss: Twice as much; at twice the usual amount.
examples: Taxis charge *double* after midnight.
Workers get paid *double* on holidays.
I had to pay *double* for a last-minute ticket.

senses.gloss: In two, or so that one thing looks like two.
examples: After the hit to the head, he was seeing *double*.
Fold the sheet *double* before you cut it.
She was bent *double* with laughter.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle

senses.gloss: Twice as much; for two reasons or in two ways.
examples: After the break-in, we were *doubly* careful to lock the door.
It's *doubly* important to drink water in this heat.
The loss was *doubly* painful because it came at home.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are not sure or do not quite believe something.
examples: She looked *doubtfully* at the old ladder.
"I guess it could work," he said *doubtfully*.
The customer eyed the price tag *doubtfully*.

position: end — after the verb or its object
modifies: verbs of moving, throwing and kicking

senses.gloss: Toward the opponent's end of a sports field.
examples: The quarterback threw the ball *downfield*.
He broke a tackle and raced *downfield*.
She passed the ball *downfield* to an open teammate.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*downright rude*)

senses.gloss: Completely; used to stress that something is bad or surprising.
examples: The service was slow and *downright* rude.
Some of the comments were *downright* offensive.
Driving in that snow was *downright* dangerous.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position

senses.gloss: In the direction a river flows; farther along the river toward its mouth.
examples: We floated *downriver* on inner tubes.
The town is about ten miles *downriver*.
The logs were carried *downriver* to the mill.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position
contrast: *Downstage* is toward the audience, not lower down; *upstage* is away from the audience. Stage left and right are also given from the actor's point of view.

senses.gloss: Toward the front of a stage, nearer the audience.
examples: The actor walked *downstage* and spoke straight to the audience.
Take two steps *downstage* so the light catches your face.
The piano sits *downstage* left.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position, often with *of*
modifies: verbs of motion and position (*downwind of the fire*)

senses.gloss: In the direction the wind is blowing.
examples: The smoke drifted *downwind* toward the highway.
Hunters try to stay *downwind* of the deer.
People living *downwind* of the plant complained about the smell.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*dreadfully sorry*); end after a verb in the 'badly' sense

senses.gloss: Very; extremely (a little old-fashioned).
examples: I'm *dreadfully* sorry for the mix-up.
It's *dreadfully* hot in here.
The house felt *dreadfully* empty after the kids left.

senses.gloss: Very badly.
examples: The actors performed *dreadfully*.
He treated his staff *dreadfully*.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that shows your mind is on pleasant thoughts rather than on what is around you.
examples: She gazed *dreamily* out the window.
"I'd love to live by the ocean," he said *dreamily*.
The kids sighed *dreamily* at the thought of summer.

position: before its word — before *wet*
form: the -ing form of *drip*, used as an intensifier
contrast: Only *dripping wet* is adverbial. In *a dripping faucet* it is a participle, and in *He was dripping with sweat* it is the verb.

senses.gloss: Extremely, in *dripping wet*: so wet that water runs off.
examples: We came in from the storm *dripping* wet.
The dog climbed out of the lake *dripping* wet and shook itself.
Her hair was still *dripping* wet from the shower.

position: before its word — only before a few adjectives, mainly *gorgeous*
form: compound of *drop* + *dead* — 'so striking you could drop dead'

senses.gloss: Extremely; used informally to praise how someone or something looks.
examples: She looked *drop-dead* gorgeous in that dress.
The view from the terrace is *drop-dead* beautiful.
Her new boyfriend is *drop-dead* handsome.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a sleepy, half-awake way.
examples: He blinked *drowsily* at the alarm clock.
"What time is it?" she asked *drowsily*.
The cat stretched *drowsily* in the sun.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: In the way a drunk person behaves.
examples: Two fans were singing *drunkenly* outside the bar.
He stumbled *drunkenly* up the stairs.
She *drunkenly* insisted that she could drive.

position: end — after a verb of speaking; mid before the verb
contrast: American spelling prefers *dryly*; *drily* is more common in British writing. Russian *сухо* often means 'coldly'; English *dryly* usually signals deadpan humor or sarcasm.

senses.gloss: In a flat, unemotional way that hides humor or sarcasm.
examples: "Well, that went well," she said *dryly*.
He *dryly* noted that the meeting could have been an email.
The report *dryly* lists the company's many failures.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with participles (*dubiously obtained*)
modifies: verbs of saying and looking; participles

senses.gloss: With doubt or suspicion.
examples: She looked *dubiously* at the gray meat.
"You fixed it yourself?" he asked *dubiously*.

senses.gloss: In a way that is questionable or probably dishonest.
examples: The money was *dubiously* obtained.
The pills are *dubiously* marketed as a cure for anxiety.

position: before its word — before *north*, *south*, *east* or *west*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *due*
contrast: Only before a compass point. *Due* in *The rent is due* is an adjective, and *due to* (*due to the rain*) works as a preposition — both belong to other dictionaries.

senses.gloss: Exactly in the direction of a compass point.
examples: The trail runs *due* north from the lake.
Sail *due* west for about two miles.
The storm is moving *due* east.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: Not sharply or brightly: with a low sound, a weak light, or a steady ache.
examples: My knee ached *dully* all afternoon.
The old coins gleamed *dully* in the case.
The door thudded *dully* behind him.

senses.gloss: Without interest or energy.
examples: He stared *dully* at the TV.
She answered *dully*, as if she hadn't slept.

position: mid — before the main verb or the past participle
modifies: verbs, often in the passive, and participles (*duly elected*)

senses.gloss: In the proper or expected way; as required.
examples: The forms were *duly* signed and returned.
He is a *duly* elected member of the board.
I asked for a refund, and it *duly* arrived a week later.

position: end — after the verb
contrast: In American English *dumb* usually means 'stupid', so *dumbly* can also sound like 'stupidly'. The 'speechless' meaning survives mainly with *stare*, *nod* and *stand*.

senses.gloss: Silently, because you are too shocked, confused or upset to speak.
examples: She nodded *dumbly*, unable to find the words.
We stared *dumbly* at the wreckage.
He stood there *dumbly* while they read the verdict.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Because it is expected of you, not because you really want to.
examples: The kids *dutifully* wrote thank-you notes.
Reporters *dutifully* copied down every number.
He laughed *dutifully* at his boss's jokes.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that keeps changing and adjusting as things happen, or with a lot of energy.
examples: The page is generated *dynamically* from the database.
Prices change *dynamically* based on demand.
The city is growing *dynamically*.

position: before its word — directly before the examples, usually after a comma or inside parentheses
form: abbreviation of Latin *exempli gratia* 'for the sake of example'
contrast: *E.g.* gives examples from a larger group; *i.e.* 'that is' restates exactly: *citrus fruit, e.g., lemons* but *the capital, i.e., Moscow*. American style puts a comma after both. In speech say *for example*.

senses.gloss: For example; used in writing before one or more examples.
examples: Bring something warm to wear (*e.g.*, a jacket or sweater).
Avoid sugary drinks, *e.g.*, soda and sports drinks.
Some fruits, *e.g.*, bananas and avocados, keep ripening after they're picked.

position: after its word — after an amount (*twenty dollars each*)
contrast: Russian puts *по* before the number (*по двадцать долларов*); English puts *each* after it: *twenty dollars each*, never *each twenty dollars*. *Each* before a noun (*each ticket*) is a determiner, covered in that dictionary.

senses.gloss: For, to or from every one of a group; apiece.
examples: The tickets are twenty dollars *each*.
The kids got two cookies *each*.
The two teams scored three goals *each*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: With strong interest, wanting very much to do or have something.
examples: The *eagerly* awaited sequel comes out Friday.
The kids ran *eagerly* to the door.
She *eagerly* agreed to help.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs of speaking, hoping and asking

senses.gloss: Seriously and sincerely, with strong feeling.
examples: He spoke *earnestly* about the need for change.
I *earnestly* hope you'll reconsider.
She looked at me *earnestly* and asked for the truth.

type: manner; also degree (*easily the best*) and stance (*could easily happen*)
position: end — after the verb or its object; before its word before a superlative or a number; mid after a modal (*could easily*)
modifies: verbs, superlatives, numbers, and modal verbs
contrast: Informal American speech keeps flat *easy* in set phrases — *take it easy*, *go easy on him*, *easier said than done* — but after most verbs the adverb is *easily*: *She won easily*, not *She won easy*.

senses.gloss: Without difficulty.
examples: She passed the test *easily*.
This recipe can *easily* be doubled.
I don't get lost *easily*.

senses.gloss: Without any doubt; by far.
examples: It was *easily* the best meal of the trip.
The crowd was *easily* ten thousand people.

senses.gloss: Very possibly; quite likely.
examples: That could *easily* happen to anyone.
The trip could *easily* take longer than we planned.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position
form: flat — the same form as the noun and adjective *east*
contrast: No preposition before the adverb: *head east*, not *head to east*. With *the* it is a noun: *in the east*, *to the east of the city*.

senses.gloss: Toward or in the east.
examples: We drove *east* for three hours.
The house faces *east*, so we get the morning sun.
The town is twenty miles *east* of Denver.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with participles (*eccentrically dressed*)

senses.gloss: In an unusual, odd way that is different from what most people do.
examples: He was *eccentrically* dressed in a cape and a top hat.
The old professor behaved *eccentrically* but was always kind.
The house was decorated *eccentrically*, with clocks on every wall.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*ecologically sound*); front as a comment
contrast: Russian *экологически чистый* is usually *environmentally friendly* or *eco-friendly* in English, not *ecologically clean*.

senses.gloss: In terms of the environment and how living things depend on it.
examples: The wetlands are *ecologically* important for migrating birds.
Is this farming method *ecologically* sustainable?
*Ecologically*, the dam was a disaster.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with *happy*

senses.gloss: With great joy and excitement.
examples: The crowd cheered *ecstatically* when the winning run scored.
She hugged him *ecstatically*.
They were *ecstatically* happy with the new baby.

position: end — after the verb or its object
modifies: *get a word in*, and verbs of moving and turning
contrast: American English says *edgewise*; British English says *edgeways*.

senses.gloss: Used in *get a word in edgewise*: to manage to say something while someone else talks nonstop.
examples: My aunt talked so much that I couldn't get a word in *edgewise*.
Let someone else get a word in *edgewise* for once.

senses.gloss: With the edge first; sideways.
examples: We had to carry the table in *edgewise*.
Turn the board *edgewise* to get it through the door.

ru: с редакционной точки зрения; в редакционной статье
position: before its word — before an adjective (*editorially independent*); end after a verb; front as a comment

senses.gloss: In terms of editing, or of a newspaper's official opinion.
examples: The magazine is *editorially* independent of its owners.
The paper argued *editorially* against the new stadium.
*Editorially*, the book still needs a lot of work.

position: before its word — before an adjective; front as a comment

senses.gloss: In terms of education or learning.
examples: The trip was fun and *educationally* valuable.
The program helps *educationally* disadvantaged children.
*Educationally*, the move was good for the kids.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*eerily quiet*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a strange, slightly frightening way.
examples: The streets were *eerily* quiet after the storm.
The two photos are *eerily* similar.
The wind howled *eerily* through the trees.

position: end — after the verb or its object in the 'well' sense; mid or before its word in the 'in fact' sense
contrast: Russian *эффективно* covers only the first sense. In *The company was effectively bankrupt*, *effectively* means 'in reality, though not officially' — *фактически*, not *эффективно*.

senses.gloss: In a way that works well and gets the result you want.
examples: She manages her time very *effectively*.
We need to communicate more *effectively* with customers.

senses.gloss: In fact, even if not officially; virtually.
examples: The decision *effectively* ends his career.
With two minutes left, the game was *effectively* over.
The road is *effectively* closed until spring.

position: end — after the verb or its object
contrast: *Efficiently* is about not wasting time, money or energy; *effectively* is about getting the result. Russian *эффективно* is used for both.

senses.gloss: Well and quickly, without wasting time, money or energy.
examples: The new engine uses fuel more *efficiently*.
The staff worked quickly and *efficiently*.
We need to run the office more *efficiently*.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Easily, so that something hard looks as if it takes no effort.
examples: She switched *effortlessly* between English and Spanish.
The dancers moved *effortlessly* across the stage.
He *effortlessly* lifted the box onto the top shelf.

position: end — after the verb or its object

senses.gloss: With a lot of warm, emotional words, sometimes more than seems sincere.
examples: She thanked us *effusively* for the flowers.
Critics praised the film *effusively*.
He apologized *effusively* for being late.

position: before its word — before a participle (*elaborately decorated*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: With a lot of careful detail.
examples: The cake was *elaborately* decorated with sugar flowers.
They planned the surprise party *elaborately*.
The dancers wore *elaborately* embroidered costumes.

position: before its word — before a participle (*electrically powered*); end after a verb

senses.gloss: By means of electricity, or in terms of electricity.
examples: The gates are *electrically* operated.
Most of the trains are *electrically* powered.
The wires must be *electrically* insulated.

position: end — after the verb or its object

senses.gloss: By computer or other electronic means.
examples: You can file your taxes *electronically*.
The documents were signed *electronically*.
Payments are sent *electronically* every two weeks.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with participles (*elegantly dressed*)

senses.gloss: In a stylish, graceful way; also, in a clever and simple way.
examples: She was *elegantly* dressed in black.
The room is *elegantly* furnished.
The new design solves the problem *elegantly*.

position: end — after the verb or its object
modifies: verbs of speaking, writing and showing

senses.gloss: In a clear, powerful and moving way, especially in speech or writing.
examples: She spoke *eloquently* about her years as a nurse.
The photos show the cost of war more *eloquently* than any speech.
He argued his case *eloquently*.

position: before its word — before an adjective; front as a comment on the whole sentence

senses.gloss: To a degree that makes you feel awkward or ashamed.
examples: The answer was *embarrassingly* simple.
We lost by an *embarrassingly* wide margin.
*Embarrassingly*, I had forgotten her name.

position: before its word — before an adjective
contrast: Do not confuse with *imminently* 'very soon, about to happen': *eminently qualified*, but *a storm is imminent*.

senses.gloss: Very; used to stress a good quality.
examples: She is *eminently* qualified for the job.
That seems like an *eminently* reasonable request.
The book is *eminently* readable.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you understand how someone else feels.
examples: The nurse listened *empathetically* as he described the pain.
She nodded *empathetically*.
Good managers respond *empathetically* when employees struggle.

position: mid or end; before its word before *not* (*emphatically not*)

senses.gloss: Strongly and clearly, leaving no doubt.
examples: The mayor *emphatically* denied the rumors.
"No," she said *emphatically*.
This is *emphatically* not the time to quit.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with participles (*empirically tested*)

senses.gloss: By observation and experiment rather than by theory.
examples: The idea has never been tested *empirically*.
Their claims are *empirically* supported by years of data.
Researchers set out to measure the effect *empirically*.

position: end — after the verb; front as a comment on the whole sentence

senses.gloss: In a way that gives someone hope or confidence.
examples: The coach smiled *encouragingly* at the nervous player.
"You're almost there," she said *encouragingly*.
*Encouragingly*, sales rose for the third month in a row.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*endearingly awkward*)

senses.gloss: In a way that makes people like someone, often in spite of a small flaw.
examples: He was *endearingly* awkward on their first date.
The puppy is *endearingly* clumsy.
Her notes are full of *endearingly* bad drawings.

position: end — after the verb; before its word before an adjective

senses.gloss: Without stopping, or seeming never to stop.
examples: My brother talks *endlessly* about football.
The debate went on *endlessly*.
I find the city *endlessly* fascinating.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*enduringly popular*)

senses.gloss: In a way that lasts for a long time.
examples: The song has stayed *enduringly* popular for fifty years.
Her novels have proved *enduringly* influential.
It's one of the most *enduringly* successful shows on TV.

position: end — after the verb or its object

senses.gloss: With a lot of energy and effort.
examples: The kids danced *energetically* to the music.
She campaigned *energetically* for the new park.
He scrubbed the pan *energetically*.

position: end — after the verb; before its word with participles (*engagingly written*)
modifies: verbs of speaking and writing; participles and adjectives

senses.gloss: In a pleasant, charming way that holds your attention.
examples: The book is *engagingly* written and easy to follow.
She spoke *engagingly* about her years in Alaska.
He smiled *engagingly* and asked for one more chance.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a mysterious way that is hard to understand or explain.
examples: She smiled *enigmatically* and said nothing.
"You'll see," he replied *enigmatically*.
The note was *enigmatically* signed with a single initial.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: With great excitement and interest.
examples: The audience applauded *enthusiastically*.
She *enthusiastically* agreed to join the band.
Voters responded *enthusiastically* to the plan.

position: before its word — before an adjective
contrast: *Enviably* describes something other people would like to have (*enviably fit*). *Enviously* describes the person who feels the envy (*She looked at him enviously*).

senses.gloss: To a degree that makes other people wish they had the same.
examples: She stays *enviably* calm under pressure.
At sixty, he's still *enviably* fit.
They live on an *enviably* quiet street.

position: end — after the verb

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you wish you had what someone else has.
examples: He looked *enviously* at his friend's new car.
The younger kids watched *enviously* from the sidelines.
"Must be nice," she said *enviously*.

type: degree; also manner (*split it equally*) and linking (*Equally, ...*)
position: before its word — before an adjective or adverb (*equally good*); end after a verb (*share equally*)
contrast: *Equally as* (*equally as good*) is common in speech, but careful writers drop *as*: *equally good*, or *just as good*.

senses.gloss: To the same degree or extent.
examples: Both candidates are *equally* qualified.
Diet and exercise are *equally* important.
The two methods work *equally* well.

senses.gloss: In equal parts, or in the same way for everyone.
examples: We split the bill *equally*.

position: end — after the verb or its object

senses.gloss: Fairly, so that everyone gets a reasonable share.
examples: The money will be distributed *equitably* among the schools.

position: front — at the start of the result clause, usually after a comma or semicolon

contrast: It sounds bookish or mock-logical. In everyday speech say *so*, and in writing *therefore*.

senses.gloss: Therefore; used to introduce a logical result.
examples: He lied under oath; *ergo*, he can't be trusted.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle (*erotically charged*); end after a verb

position: mid — before the main verb or the past participle (*erroneously reported*)

ru: и т. д., и так далее
position: end — at the end of a list, after a comma

contrast: Never *and etc.* — *et* already means 'and'. Do not end a list with *etc.* after *such as*, *e.g.* or *including*, which already say the list is incomplete. Read aloud it is *et cetera*, with a *t* sound, not *ek-cetera*.

senses.gloss: And other things of the same kind; and so on.
